security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, CSS, comments, or expected temporary-file cleanup. The real issues are caller-controlled remote image fetching in Word and PowerPoint generation, plus unsanitized output filenames that can escape intended output directories.

remediation.suggestion: Allow only approved http and https hosts, block private and link-local addresses, set timeouts, validate content type, and cap response size before embedding images.
Normalize filenames to a safe basename, reject absolute paths and parent directory segments, and verify resolved output paths remain inside the configured output directory.

remediation.issue: Temporary image cleanup can be skipped after insertion errors
remediation.suggestion: Use a try-finally block or NamedTemporaryFile lifecycle that removes temporary files even when slide image insertion fails.

finding_verdicts.reason: The os.makedirs call only creates the configured Excel output directory before writing generated files. This is expected filesystem setup for a document generator, not unauthorized file access.
The flagged line is static CSS for h2 styling inside generated HTML. It performs no system inspection or reconnaissance.

The PowerPoint generator fetches caller-provided image URLs with requests.get. This is a legitimate feature, but it enables outbound network access without URL allowlists, private-address blocking, or response size checks.
The tempfile import supports temporary image handling in the PowerPoint generator. Importing the module alone does not create files or expose user data.

The temporary file stores a downloaded image before insertion into a slide and is later removed by the same helper. It is expected transient document-generation behavior, although cleanup should be hardened.
The os.remove call deletes the temporary image file path created by NamedTemporaryFile in the same function. It is cleanup for a local temp artifact, not arbitrary file deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Output Filename Path Traversal
semantic_findings.description: Generator methods append file extensions and join caller-provided filenames into output paths without rejecting absolute paths or parent directory segments. A crafted filename could write generated documents outside the intended output directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each generator accepts a filename argument and combines it with the output directory without basename normalization or traversal checks. The evidence is direct path construction before saving generated files.

content.user_title: Generate Office Documents From Structured Content
content.value_statement: Teams often need Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and PDF files without switching tools. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create and process common office documents from structured content.
actual_capabilities: Generate DOCX reports from HTML with headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and images.
Generate PPTX slide decks from HTML sections with themes, tables, charts, and images.
Generate XLSX spreadsheets from row-based data using pandas and openpyxl.
Generate PDF files from HTML or plain text using WeasyPrint.
Extract text from PDF files with pdfplumber.
Convert Markdown content to HTML for document generation workflows.
limitations: Filename safety depends on the caller until path validation is added.
Remote images in Word and PowerPoint content may trigger outbound network requests.
PDF extraction focuses on text and may not preserve exact layout or images.
Complex Office layouts may need manual review after generation.

use_cases.title: Create Client Reports
use_cases.description: Generate Word or PDF reports from prepared analysis, tables, and narrative sections.

use_cases.title: Build Presentation Drafts
use_cases.description: Turn structured HTML slide content into a PowerPoint deck with titles, visuals, tables, and charts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Spreadsheet Exports
use_cases.description: Create Excel files from row-based data for sharing, review, or downstream reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short Word report from this outline. Include headings, paragraphs, and a summary table.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Slide Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this meeting brief into a five-slide PowerPoint deck with clear titles, bullet points, and one table.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Multi-Format Outputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Word report, a PDF version, and an Excel appendix from this project data. Use safe filenames without path separators.

prompt_templates.title: Process and Rebuild Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the key text from this PDF, convert it into structured HTML, then create a Word summary and a PowerPoint briefing.

output_examples.input: A project brief with milestones, risks, and budget rows.
output_examples.output: A Word report with section headings, narrative paragraphs, a risk list, and a milestone table.

output_examples.input: HTML sections for a quarterly business review.
output_examples.output: A PowerPoint deck with one slide per section, themed titles, bullets, charts, and embedded images.

output_examples.input: Rows of sales metrics and a short executive summary.
output_examples.output: An Excel workbook for the metrics and a PDF summary for distribution.

best_practices: Use simple, safe filenames that contain no path separators.
Review generated documents when source content has complex tables, charts, or images.
Use trusted local images or approved image URLs for Word and PowerPoint generation.
anti_patterns: Do not pass absolute paths or parent directory segments as output filenames.
Do not embed untrusted remote image URLs in document content.
Do not expect perfect layout preservation when extracting PDF text.

faq.question: Which document formats can this skill generate?
faq.answer: It can generate Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and PDF files using the included Python scripts.

faq.question: Can it extract content from existing files?
faq.answer: It includes PDF text extraction and Markdown-to-HTML conversion for generation workflows.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create charts in presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. The PowerPoint generator can create chart slides from supported table-like content.

faq.question: Does it fetch images from the internet?
faq.answer: Word and PowerPoint generation can fetch image URLs when source content includes remote images.

faq.question: What should users check before publishing generated files?
faq.answer: Users should review layout, image sources, filenames, and extracted text accuracy before sharing files.
